WavePaintings.name: Wave Paintings
WavePaintings.description: Three pendulum-painting stations—grab the bob to swing it, watch oscillation become visible trace. Each pendulum paints on a wet canvas below, translating harmonic motion into color trails. The physics of swinging becomes the brush; chaos becomes art.
WavePaintings.qfep_connection: Oscillation as the fundamental pattern of non-rest — perpetual movement between poles. The simplest E(S) that isn't random: structured, predictable, yet never still. Painting makes the wave's F-structure visible as trace.

foucault_pendulum.name: Foucault Pendulum
foucault_pendulum.description: A brass pendulum swings from high above, drawing rosette patterns on a cream canvas below. The swing plane slowly precesses—Foucault's elegant proof that Earth rotates beneath us. Dark ink traces accumulate into intricate spirograph-like figures over time.
foucault_pendulum.qfep_connection: The pendulum maintains its F (swing plane) while the frame rotates beneath it. Inertia as F-preservation — the system resists external perturbation, holding its internal model constant against a changing reference frame.

VitruvianMan.name: Vitruvian Man
VitruvianMan.description: Da Vinci's proportional man reinterpreted—the human body inscribed in circle and square, demonstrating that anatomy is geometry, that limbs sweep arcs, that the body itself is a measurement system oscillating between ideal forms.

SoundBoxLong.name: Sound Box (Long)
SoundBoxLong.description: Extended resonant chamber—a longer tube means lower fundamental frequency. This is why cellos are larger than violins: wavelength determines pitch, and pitch determines the physical size of instruments.

SoundBoxShort.name: Sound Box (Short)
SoundBoxShort.description: Compact resonant chamber—a shorter tube means higher fundamental frequency. The relationship between length and pitch is the physical basis of all wind and string instruments.

spectrum_display.name: Frequency Spectrum Analyzer
spectrum_display.description: Displays frequency spectrum as vertical bars showing audio content from 0-8kHz

spectral_sine_wave.name: Spectral Sine Wave
spectral_sine_wave.description: Visualizes frequency spectrum as a sine wave where amplitude is modulated by spectral content over time

walkable_sine_bridge.name: walkable_sine_bridge
walkable_sine_bridge.description: Extrudes a walkable ribbon along a sine wave, adds supports, and spawns a player on the path.

DancingBody.name: Dancing Body
DancingBody.description: Kinematic waves—sine functions propagated through a skeletal hierarchy create procedural dance. The body becomes an instrument played by oscillation; movement emerges from phase lag down the bone chain.

OscillatingWave.name: Oscillating Wave
OscillatingWave.description: The fundamental wave made visible—a 3D sine wave oscillating in real-time. Adjust amplitude, frequency, and phase to feel how these parameters shape the perpetual motion between poles.
OscillatingWave.qfep_connection: The pure sine wave is the atom of periodic E(S) — the simplest non-trivial dynamics. Amplitude, frequency, and phase are the three parameters that fully describe it: maximum F-compression of oscillatory behavior.

HarmonicBuilder.name: Harmonic Builder
HarmonicBuilder.description: Fourier synthesis in action—stack sine waves of different frequencies to build complex shapes. Any waveform is a sum of simple oscillations; this tool lets you construct them one harmonic at a time.
HarmonicBuilder.qfep_connection: Fourier synthesis as F-construction — building complex waveforms from simple components. Each harmonic adds E(S); the sum approaches any target shape. Complexity from simplicity, order from the accumulation of periodic structures.

BeatFrequencies.name: Beat Frequencies
BeatFrequencies.description: When two waves of slightly different frequency combine, they create a pulsing envelope—the 'beat'. This is how piano tuners work, how interference patterns form, how waves negotiate difference.
BeatFrequencies.qfep_connection: Two nearly-identical F-models interfering — the beat frequency emerges from their difference. Small λ-deviation produces slow pulsing; large deviation produces rapid oscillation. Difference itself becomes a wave.

ColoredLinesVR.name: ColoredLinesVR
ColoredLinesVR.description: Builds a VR hallway filled with glowing sine-wave tubes rendered from procedural meshes.

StaticCables.name: StaticCables
StaticCables.description: Creates suspended cable bundles with configurable sag, wave, or spiral patterns and foggy lighting.

pylon_cables.name: Electric Pylon Cables
pylon_cables.description: Four electric pylons with swinging cables between them. Cables sway in the wind. Final cable drops to a transformer box on the ground. Lattice tower construction with insulators.

doublehelix.name: doublehelix
doublehelix.description: Procedurally models an adjustable DNA-style double helix with strands, rungs, and rebuild-on-change controls.

dual_display_test.name: dual_display_test
dual_display_test.description: Visualizes frequency spectrum as a sine wave where amplitude is modulated by spectral content over time

fourier_transform.name: Fourier Transform
fourier_transform.description: Frequency domain analysis and signal processing
fourier_transform.qfep_connection: The Fourier transform IS a change of F-basis — decomposing a complex signal into its frequency components. Time-domain complexity becomes frequency-domain order. The ultimate F-minimization: any signal reduced to amplitudes and phases.

resonance_frequencies_visualizer.name: Resonance Frequencies Visualizer
resonance_frequencies_visualizer.description: Every object has frequencies at which it wants to vibrate—its resonant modes. This visualizer reveals those hidden harmonics, showing how systems amplify certain frequencies while damping others. Resonance is selective listening.
resonance_frequencies_visualizer.qfep_connection: Resonance as F-alignment — the system's natural modes are where external energy couples most efficiently. At resonance, minimal input produces maximal response because the drive matches the system's internal F-model.

unit_circle.name: Unit Circle
unit_circle.description: Trigonometric functions visualization on unit circle
unit_circle.qfep_connection: The unit circle is the F-generator for all periodic motion — sin and cos as the fundamental basis functions. Rotation on the circle maps to oscillation on the line; phase space geometry produces temporal dynamics.

tech_noir_audio.name: Tech Noir Audio
tech_noir_audio.description: John Cage inspired algorithmic audio composition

liturgicalambientgen.name: liturgicalambientgenera
liturgicalambientgen.description: Threaded ambient generator that layers choral drones, organ swells, and cathedral effects with progress visualization.

noir_sequencer.name: Noir Sequencer
noir_sequencer.description: Film noir style algorithmic music sequencer

SphericalHarmonics.name: Spherical Harmonics
SphericalHarmonics.description: Waves on a sphere—the mathematical functions that describe electron orbitals, planetary magnetic fields, and 3D audio spatialization. These are the 3D cousins of sine waves, oscillating across spherical surfaces.
SphericalHarmonics.qfep_connection: Spherical harmonics are the F-basis for any function on a sphere — the most compressed representation of spherical complexity. Electron orbitals, planetary fields, and audio all share these same fundamental modes of order.

kusama_sine.name: Kusama Sine
kusama_sine.description: Yayoi Kusama inspired sine wave patterns

john_cage_tech_noir.name: john_cage_tech_noir
john_cage_tech_noir.description: Procedurally composes endless techno-noir ambience with city drones, random effects, and a loading-bar visualizer.

mario_test_sound_ui.name: mario_test_sound_ui
mario_test_sound_ui.description: Sci-fi kiosk hosting a VR map-loader station UI with sequence and algorithm filters.

vr_map_loader_kiosk.name: VR Map Loader Kiosk
vr_map_loader_kiosk.description: VR loading station for maps. Filter by sequence and algorithm, then load one map at a time from the kiosk screen.

DualBallFMController.name: Dual Ball FM Synth
DualBallFMController.description: Two-handed FM synthesis controller using ValueMapper3D balls. Blue ball controls carrier (frequency, attack, decay); orange ball controls modulator (ratio, index, decay). Classic FM synthesis—one oscillator modulating another's phase to create bells, metallic textures, electric pianos, brass. Presets for common FM patches.

coshlea.name: coshlea
coshlea.description: Creates a hyperbolic cosine helicoid surface with adjustable domain sampling.

sine_cylinder_staircase.name: sine_cylinder_staircase
sine_cylinder_staircase.description: Builds a helical staircase around a central column, modulating tread radius with a sine wave.

sine_wall_static.name: Sine Wall (Static)
sine_wall_static.description: Architecture frozen mid-oscillation—a wall whose surface undulates in a sine pattern. This is what waves look like when time stops: pure spatial frequency without temporal change.

sine_art_monitor.name: Sine Art Monitor
sine_art_monitor.description: Wave as artwork—a display showing sine functions rendered as visual compositions. The same mathematics that describes sound and light becomes aesthetic object.

sine_wall_corridor.name: Sine Wall Corridor
sine_wall_corridor.description: A passageway bounded by undulating walls—walking through is walking through a frozen wave. The body experiences wavelength as architectural scale.

SplineCables.name: Spline Cables
SplineCables.description: Smooth curves connecting points—cables that hang in catenary arcs, the natural shape a flexible line takes under gravity. Infrastructure as frozen wave.

lissajous_curves.name: LissajousCurves
lissajous_curves.qfep_connection: Two orthogonal oscillations creating complex figures — the ratio of frequencies determines the pattern. Rational ratios produce closed curves (low F), irrational ratios produce space-filling chaos (high E(S)). Commensurability as order.

coupled_oscillator_lattice.name: CoupledOscillatorLattice
coupled_oscillator_lattice.qfep_connection: Coupled oscillators demonstrate how local F-interactions propagate into global wave patterns. Each oscillator only knows its neighbors, yet collective modes emerge — local order generating distributed E(S) dynamics.

rainbow_hallway.name: rainbow_hallway
rainbow_hallway.description: CSG hallway coated with animated rainbow shader controls and glow-rich lighting.

hallway_scene.name: hallway_scene
hallway_scene.description: Populates a tunnel with sine-driven cylinder tubes and animates them through time.

segment_slide.name: Segment Slide
segment_slide.description: A ride segment following wave contours—slide down a sine curve, feel acceleration as slope changes. The body learns wave mathematics through gravity and motion.

resonating_metallophone.name: Resonating Metallophone
resonating_metallophone.description: Metal bars that ring—each bar's length determines its pitch, shorter bars vibrate faster. Strike them to hear wavelength become sound, to feel the relationship between physical size and frequency.

line_builder_3d.name: Line Builder 3D
line_builder_3d.description: Draw curves in space—each line segment becomes a building block for wave forms. Connect points to see how discrete positions approximate continuous curves.

cable_builder.name: Cable Builder
cable_builder.description: Construct hanging cables between anchor points—watch them sag into catenaries, the natural curve of flexible lines under gravity. Engineering meets wave mathematics.

DoublePendulum.name: Double Pendulum
DoublePendulum.description: Deterministic chaos—two connected pendulums create wildly unpredictable motion from simple physics. This is where periodic oscillation breaks down; tiny differences in starting conditions lead to radically different trajectories.
DoublePendulum.qfep_connection: The double pendulum is where simple F breaks — two connected oscillators produce chaotic trajectories with positive Lyapunov exponents. The system is deterministic but unpredictable: the φΔE(S,t) term dominates as sensitivity to initial conditions.

PendulumGrid3x3.name: Pendulum Grid 3x3
PendulumGrid3x3.description: Nine pendulums in a grid—each swinging independently but visible together. Watch for emergent patterns: when do they synchronize? When do they diverge? Collective oscillation reveals hidden coupling.

math_objects.name: Mathematical Objects
math_objects.description: A collection of parametric surfaces and curves—the geometric zoo of mathematical forms. Tori, helicoids, Möbius strips: shapes defined by equations rather than construction.

CircleSpiral.name: Circle Spiral
CircleSpiral.description: Rotation extended through time becomes spiral—a circle that doesn't close but climbs. This is what happens when circular motion gains a third dimension: the helix, the spring, the DNA strand.

standing_waves.name: Standing Waves
standing_waves.qfep_connection: Standing waves are where two opposing wave-flows reach equilibrium — nodes of zero motion amid maximum oscillation. The system finds stable F-patterns within dynamic E(S): stillness emerging from movement.

SimpleOscillatingBridge.name: Simple Oscillating Bridge
SimpleOscillatingBridge.description: A walkable surface that breathes—rising and falling in sine wave motion. Cross it to feel oscillation in your body, the ground itself becoming unstable in a predictable rhythm.

SystemsMusicTest.name: Systems Music Test
SystemsMusicTest.description: Music as system—notes triggered by spatial position, harmony emerging from movement through space. Steve Reich meets VR: phase relationships create texture.

ruth_asawa_sculpture.name: Ruth Asawa Sculpture
ruth_asawa_sculpture.description: Wire forms inspired by Ruth Asawa's crocheted metal sculptures—nested surfaces that oscillate between inside and outside, solid and void. Topology as frozen wave, material as line drawing in space.

ElphabaDemo.name: Elphaba Demo
ElphabaDemo.description: Character animation driven by oscillation—the Wicked witch moves through wave functions. Procedural performance where sine waves become gesture, mathematics becomes drama.

ElphabaDress.name: Elphaba Dress
ElphabaDress.description: Cloth simulation as wave—fabric responds to movement with ripples propagating outward. The dress becomes a visible record of motion, trailing oscillations behind every gesture.

wave_interference.name: Wave Interference
wave_interference.qfep_connection: Superposition as entropy interaction — two ordered waves combine to create complex interference. Constructive = F-alignment (waves reinforce), destructive = F-cancellation (waves annihilate). The linearity principle in action.

fouriertransformshape.name: fouriertransformshape
fouriertransformshape.description: Shows nested rotating circles that trace a Fourier drawing with emissive connections.

wave_propagation_3d.name: 3D Wave Propagation
wave_propagation_3d.qfep_connection: Waves propagating through 3D space — energy spreading from a source, dissipating as it expands. The inverse-square law as entropy increase: concentrated E(S) becoming diffuse, order radiating into the surrounding volume.

MelodySoundBoard.name: MelodySoundBoard
MelodySoundBoard.description: Spatial musical instrument where notes are positioned in 3D space and melodies play by moving through them

MelodyChaser3D.name: MelodyChaser3D
MelodyChaser3D.description: Follow-the-leader musical instrument - a glowing point traces a helix pattern through pitch space, play notes by following it with your hand

UnitCircleTrig.name: UnitCircleTrig
UnitCircleTrig.description: Unit circle generating Sine and Cosine

TrigWalkingPath.name: TrigWalkingPath
TrigWalkingPath.description: Walkable path generated by trig functions

PendulumCircle.name: PendulumCircle
PendulumCircle.description: Compound motion of pendulum and circle

air_music_display_case.name: Air Music Display Case
air_music_display_case.description: A 1m glass museum display case with dark walnut wood frame, containing the Air Music spatial audio system. Minimalist Scandinavian design inspired by Ferm Living. Sound is subtle and ambient—notes triggered by movement through space, phasing loops creating evolving texture.

chladni_plate.name: Chladni Plate
chladni_plate.description: Vibrating metal plate with sand particles that migrate to nodal lines, forming standing wave patterns. Auto-cycles through modes showing different resonant geometries. Ernst Chladni's classic 18th-century experiment demonstrating that sound creates visible form.
chladni_plate.qfep_connection: Matter self-organizing into F-minimal patterns under vibrational forcing. Sand finds the nodes — the zero-entropy positions where the plate doesn't vibrate. Particles seek stillness within motion: F-minimization in physical space.

GlassRack.name: Glass Rack
GlassRack.description: Modular laboratory glassware system. Configurable spiral condensers, wobbly tubes, flasks, junctions. Use #config:spiral_tube, #config:spiral_condenser, #config:distillation_rack, or #config:simple_tube. Turtle path commands: f,l,r,u,d,spiral,wobbly,flask,junction.

multimeter.name: Multimeter
multimeter.description: Digital multimeter with analog-style oscillating needle. Demonstrates AC voltage waveforms—the needle deflects following sin(t * frequency), showing how alternating current oscillates between positive and negative. Modes: AC voltage, DC voltage, resistance, frequency.

chemicalapparatus.name: Chemical Apparatus
chemicalapparatus.description: Chemistry station with bubbling liquids using sine-based animation. Flask and beaker liquids oscillate with phase offsets demonstrating wave relationships. Test tubes show wave propagation. Bunsen burner flame flickers using multi-frequency sine superposition for natural randomness.

samplevialrack.name: Sample Vial Rack
samplevialrack.description: Six sample vials demonstrating phase relationships. Each vial glows with a sine wave offset by TAU/6 from its neighbor, creating a visible wave propagation effect. Modes: linear wave travel, radial expansion from center, random phases. Classic wave interference visualization.

electronicscales.name: Electronic Scales
electronicscales.description: Laboratory scales demonstrating damped harmonic oscillation. When weighing, the display settles using e^(-bt) * sin(ωt)—exponential decay multiplied by sine. Adjustable damping factor and frequency. Shows how real oscillating systems lose energy over time.

microscope.name: Microscope
microscope.description: Laboratory microscope with pulsing illumination. Stage light breathes with slow sine wave, objective lens glows in quadrature phase. Auto-focus mode oscillates the stage height. Focus knob rotates to show mechanical-wave coupling. Three color-coded objectives.

atmosphericmonitoring.name: Atmospheric Monitoring Station
atmosphericmonitoring.description: Three analog gauges at different frequencies: pressure (0.05 Hz slow drift), temperature (0.02 Hz), humidity (0.03 Hz). Demonstrates how multiple independent oscillations create complex patterns. Status lights indicate normal ranges. Real atmospheric data oscillates similarly.

holographicdisplay.name: Holographic Display
holographicdisplay.description: Holographic projector with sine-based effects. Scan line sweeps vertically using sin(t), content rotates and bobs, flicker effect at 15Hz creates subtle instability. Wireframe cube demonstrates 3D rotation. Projector lights pulse with phase offsets around the ring.

biomagneticresonator.name: Biomagnetic Resonator
biomagneticresonator.description: Demonstrates standing waves with harmonic superposition. Core pulses at fundamental frequency while field rings show Σ(1/h)*sin(h*ω*t + φ)—each ring receives the sum of fundamental plus overtones. Adjustable harmonic count (1-8). Energy beams rotate with phase offsets.

static_reference_cube.name: Static Reference Cube
static_reference_cube.description: Stage 1 of oscillation progression: A motionless cube establishing the baseline for comparison. Without stillness, we cannot perceive motion. The constant against which all oscillation is measured. Position = constant, y = 0.

rotating_cube_demo.name: Rotating Cube Demo
rotating_cube_demo.description: Continuous rotation demonstration: θ += ω·dt. The simplest rotational motion—angle increases by angular velocity times delta time each frame. Ground arc shows the rotation path, direction arrow tracks the current angle. Constant spin, no oscillation.

y_oscillation_cube.name: Y-Oscillation Cube
y_oscillation_cube.description: Stage 2 of oscillation progression: Core concept of y = A·sin(ωt). A cube oscillates vertically along a rail, demonstrating how sine function maps time to position. Trail ghosts show motion path, real-time labels display t, sin(t), and y values. The fundamental oscillation.

rotation_oscillation_cube.name: Rotation Oscillation Cube
rotation_oscillation_cube.description: Stage 3 of oscillation progression: θ = A·sin(ωt) applied to rotation instead of position. Same mathematics, different output mapping. Arc indicator shows rotation range, direction arrow on cube face. Toggle between oscillating mode (pendulum-like) and continuous rotation (θ += ω·dt).

oscillation_controlled_cube.name: Oscillation Controlled Cube
oscillation_controlled_cube.description: Stage 4 of oscillation progression: The 'mario cube' responding to pendulum control. Three simultaneous mappings: y_offset → Y position, angular_velocity → rotation speed, amplitude → scale pulse. Visual guides show vertical rail, rotation arc, and real-time parameter breakdown. QFEP: One input, many outputs—oscillation as control signal.

sine_wall_explanation.name: Sine Wall Explanation
sine_wall_explanation.description: 1m display case showing how sine function shapes corridor walls. Animated mini-corridor demonstrates x = A·sin(f·z)—the wave displacement that creates the sine_wall_corridor effect. Shows amplitude, frequency parameters with live wave propagation.

sine_space_explanation.name: Sine Space Explanation
sine_space_explanation.description: 1m display case showing how sine waves modulate 3D space. An 8×8 grid of points demonstrates y = A·sin(x)·sin(z)—the product of two sine functions creating a wave surface. Points rise and fall showing phase relationships across X and Z axes.

RackSineBasic.name: Sine Wave Rack
RackSineBasic.description: Basic sine wave synthesizer rack with frequency, amplitude, and duration controls. Includes waveform display. The purest sound—a single frequency oscillating smoothly. Grab sliders in VR to shape the wave, hear mathematics become music.

Rack303Acid.name: 303 Acid Rack
Rack303Acid.description: Roland TB-303 style acid bass synthesizer with cutoff and resonance knobs. The squelchy sound that defined acid house—filter sweeps turning simple waveforms into liquid screams. Resonance creates feedback peaks at the cutoff frequency.

Rack808Drums.name: 808 Kick Rack
Rack808Drums.description: Deep 808 kick drum synthesizer with decay control and VU meter. The foundation of hip-hop and electronic music—sub-bass that you feel more than hear. Sine wave with pitch envelope creates that iconic 'boom'.

RackMario.name: Mario Pickup Rack
RackMario.description: Mario-style pickup sound synthesizer with start/end frequency sweep controls. The iconic coin sound—a rapid frequency chirp that triggers dopamine. Demonstrates how frequency modulation over time creates recognizable timbres.

RackDX7Piano.name: DX7 Piano Rack
RackDX7Piano.description: Yamaha DX7 FM electric piano synthesizer with attack and release envelope controls. The sound of the 80s—FM synthesis creating bell-like tones impossible with analog. Frequency modulation: one oscillator modulating another's frequency.

RackMoogBass.name: Moog Bass Rack
RackMoogBass.description: Classic Moog-style bass/lead synthesizer with ladder filter cutoff and resonance. The fat analog sound—oscillators through the famous 4-pole filter. Cutoff frequency determines which harmonics pass; resonance emphasizes the cutoff point.

RackAmbientDrone.name: Ambient Drone Rack
RackAmbientDrone.description: Atmospheric ambient drone synthesizer with lissajous phase display. Slowly evolving textures—sound as environment rather than event. Multiple detuned oscillators create beating patterns; the lissajous shows phase relationships between channels.

VRAudioMonitor.name: VR Audio Monitor
VRAudioMonitor.description: Standalone audio monitor display showing waveform and spectrum analysis. Place near any audio source to visualize sound. The waveform shows amplitude over time; the spectrum shows frequency content—two complementary views of the same signal.

harmonic_distance_table.name: Harmonic Distance Table
harmonic_distance_table.description: Tabletop artifact with 12 chromatic pitch nodes in circle-of-fifths layout. Grab nodes to hear intervals; spatial distance corresponds to harmonic consonance. Activate a node as tonal center to see all others recolor by harmonic function (tonic=green, dominant=blue, subdominant=yellow). Glowing overtone connection lines show shared harmonics between pitches. Cognitive compression: harmonic distance becomes a felt spatial relationship.

timbre_sculptor.name: Timbre Sculptor
timbre_sculptor.description: VR rack panel with 8 vertical sliders controlling harmonic amplitudes for real-time additive synthesis. Waveform and spectrum displays show the result. Preset buttons morph to known timbres: sine, square, sawtooth, triangle, and vowel approximations (A, E, I, O, U). Cognitive compression: timbre IS harmonic recipe — the slider heights ARE the spectrum. Build Fourier transforms with your hands.

GlassRack_BranchingCondenser.name: Glass Rack: Branching Condenser
GlassRack_BranchingCondenser.description: Y-pipe splits flow into two parallel spiral condensers, then recombines.

GlassRack_BreakingBadCoffee.name: Glass Rack: Breaking Bad Coffee
GlassRack_BreakingBadCoffee.description: Multi-level cold drip coffee / distillation apparatus with metal frame.

GlassRack_ComplexApparatus.name: Glass Rack: Complex Apparatus
GlassRack_ComplexApparatus.description: Complete reflux apparatus with boiling flask, condenser, collection vessel, and branching tubes.

GlassRack_DistillationRack.name: Glass Rack: Distillation Rack
GlassRack_DistillationRack.description: Classic distillation setup with flask, spiral condenser, and collection vessel.

GlassRack_DistillationY.name: Glass Rack: Y-Branch Distillation
GlassRack_DistillationY.description: Simple Y-branch with two spiral condensers feeding into beakers.

GlassRack_FractionalDistillation.name: Glass Rack: Fractional Distillation
GlassRack_FractionalDistillation.description: Multi-stage distillation with reducers and collection points.

GlassRack_RefluxApparatus.name: Glass Rack: Reflux Apparatus
GlassRack_RefluxApparatus.description: Flask with condenser and U-bend return for continuous reflux.

GlassRack_SbendManifold.name: Glass Rack: S-Bend Manifold
GlassRack_SbendManifold.description: Multiple S-bends creating an offset distribution manifold.

GlassRack_SimpleTube.name: Glass Rack: Simple Tube
GlassRack_SimpleTube.description: Basic straight tube with a bend.

GlassRack_SpiralCondenser.name: Glass Rack: Spiral Condenser
GlassRack_SpiralCondenser.description: Standalone spiral condenser with inlet and outlet tubes.

GlassRack_SpiralTube.name: Glass Rack: Spiral Tube
GlassRack_SpiralTube.description: Simple spiral glass tube — classic lab condenser coil.

BigPipe_LBend.name: Big Pipe: L-Bend
BigPipe_LBend.description: Right-angle corner routing with straight runs on each side.

BigPipe_TDistribution.name: Big Pipe: T-Distribution
BigPipe_TDistribution.description: Main line splits into two branches via T-junction.

BigPipe_Serpentine.name: Big Pipe: Serpentine
BigPipe_Serpentine.description: Back-and-forth pipe runs for cooling or heating pattern.

BigPipe_VerticalBypass.name: Big Pipe: Vertical Bypass
BigPipe_VerticalBypass.description: Main line with vertical up-and-over bypass loop.

BigPipe_CrossManifold.name: Big Pipe: Cross Manifold
BigPipe_CrossManifold.description: Central cross junction with four capped branches — distribution hub.

BigPipe_IndustrialBranch.name: Big Pipe: Industrial Branch
BigPipe_IndustrialBranch.description: Full demo of all pipe segments: S-bend, T-junction, cross, vertical up/down, end cap.

BigPipeSystem.name: Big Pipe System
BigPipeSystem.description: Industrial drain pipe network built from modular segments — straights, corners, T-junctions, crosses, vertical bends. Pipes as frozen flow: the physical infrastructure that channels movement. WFC-adjacent: each segment constrains its neighbors.

lab_table.name: Lab Table
lab_table.description: Procedural wooden lab table with legs and support frame. Surface for placing instruments and apparatus. The workbench where oscillation becomes experiment.

chord_tension_spring.name: Chord Tension Spring
chord_tension_spring.description: Four pitch nodes connected by visible springs. Consonant chord = springs relax, nodes settle. Dissonant chord = springs vibrate, nodes jitter. Drag nodes to change pitch and feel tension physically. Preset buttons for major, minor, dom7, dim, aug, sus4, tritone. Resolution IS relaxation.

BigPipe.name: BigPipe
BigPipe.description: Large drain pipe system with segments. Turtle commands: f,l,r,u,d,s(s-bend). Use BigPipe#path:f,f,l,f,u,f

soundboxes.name: Dynamic Sound Box
soundboxes.description: SoundBox: Procedural Sound Gallery. Use #collections:synthetic, retro, legends, drums, body, machine, synth, sacred, noir, weather, game for presets.
